_comment: Example of the document held in SSM at /porth/config/testbed. Copy, fill in, and load:
aws ssm put-parameter --name /porth/config/testbed --type SecureString \
--value file://testbed-manifest.json --overwrite --region us-east-1
It is NOT read from this repo — this file is documentation. The seed Lambda reads the
SSM parameter directly, so nothing about the testbed transits CI.
Passwords are NEVER in here. 'password_secret' is a Secrets Manager name; the seeder
only calls DescribeSecret and cannot read the value. Create each one alongside the IdP
user, which needs that provider's management API:
aws secretsmanager create-secret --name /porth/testbed/tenants/acme/password \
--secret-string '<password>' --region us-east-1
Get the three IdP URLs from the provider's discovery document rather than by hand —
the issuer must byte-match the 'iss' claim, and Auth0 has a trailing slash where
Keycloak does not:
curl -s https://<host>/.well-known/openid-configuration | jq '{issuer, jwks_uri, end_session_endpoint}'
The platform-admin identity and the IdP the BFF proxy authenticates against.
porth-install builds /porth/auth from platform.idp; the platform TENANT itself is
created by the bootstrap, not by the seeder (PORTH-536).
A second provider. No provider_org_id — Keycloak has no Auth0 Organization
equivalent, so this tenant resolves by issuer alone. Note the issuer has NO
trailing slash.
Documents the slot the Tier 2 e2e suite owns. Nothing is written for it — the test
creates this tenant itself in beforeAll and tolerates a 409. Needs no idp or admin.
This is the one place the reserved names are allowed.
